## Setup and paths
```{r setup, message=FALSE}
# Install packages
packages <- c(
  "tidyverse", "readxl", "brms", "rstan",
  "posterior", "tidybayes", "terra", "sf",
  "patchwork", "ggnewscale", "RColorBrewer",
  "ragg", "knitr", "rmarkdown"
)

missing <- setdiff(packages, rownames(installed.packages()))

if (length(missing) > 0) {
  install.packages(missing, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
} else {
  message("installed!")
}
for (pkg in packages) {
  library(pkg, character.only = TRUE)
}
# Run from the project root, or set this environment variable to that root.
project_dir <- normalizePath(Sys.getenv("ARCHAEO_BODYFORM_ROOT", "."),
                             winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_dir)

data_file <- file.path(project_dir, "data", "bodyform_data_AUDITED_v2.xlsx")

out_dir <- file.path(project_dir, "output")
audit_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "audit")
table_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "tables")
model_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "models")
fig_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "figures")
invisible(lapply(c(out_dir, audit_dir, table_dir, model_dir, fig_dir),
                 dir.create, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE))

SEED <- 42L
set.seed(SEED)
options(mc.cores = 4L)
run_sdc_sensitivity <- FALSE
fill_missing_fbl <- FALSE  # Do not change until the remaining gaps are reviewed.
prediction_ndraws <- 1000L # Use NULL to use all retained posterior draws.
prediction_chunk_cells <- 250L
grid_resolution <- 350L   # Same regular grid resolution as the supplied code.
stan_backend <- "rstan"   # Set to "cmdstanr" only if CmdStan is configured.
refit_mode <- "on_change" # Use "always" when changing sampling settings/seed.
brms_control <- list(adapt_delta = 0.99, max_treedepth = 15)
if (!requireNamespace(stan_backend, quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Install/configure the selected Stan backend: ", stan_backend)
}

PERIOD_CODES <- c("E_Neo", "M_Neo", "L_Neo", "Bronze_Early_Iron",
                  "EarlyImp", "MiddleImp", "LateImp")
PERIOD_LABELS <- c("Early Neolithic", "Middle Neolithic", "Late Neolithic",
                   "Bronze–Early Iron Age", "Early Imperial",
                   "Middle Imperial", "Late Imperial")
PERIOD_PLOT_LABELS <- c("Early\nNeolithic", "Middle\nNeolithic",
                        "Late\nNeolithic", "Bronze–Early\nIron Age",
                        "Early\nImperial", "Middle\nImperial", "Late\nImperial")
traits <- c("FXL", "FHD", "TXL", "HXL", "RXL", "BI", "CI")
climate_paths <- c(
  Mintemp = file.path(project_dir, "climatic data/wc2.1_30s_bio_6.tif"),
  Maxtemp = file.path(project_dir, "climatic data/wc2.1_30s_bio_5.tif"),
  Minprecip = file.path(project_dir, "climatic data/wc2.1_30s_bio_14.tif"),
  Maxprecip = file.path(project_dir, "climatic data/wc2.1_30s_bio_13.tif"),
  Altitude = file.path(project_dir, "climatic data/wc2.1_30s_elev.tif")
)



# Load the map data
Sys.setenv("SHAPE_RESTORE_SHX" = "YES")

# Load shapefile
chinashape <- st_read("mapdata/china.shp")
chinashape <- sf::st_set_crs(chinashape, 4326)
basemap_wgs84 <- chinashape
plot(sf::st_geometry(basemap_wgs84))
dem <- rast("mapdata/GRAY_HR_SR_W.tif")

# Ensure WGS84
if (!grepl("4326", crs(dem))) {
  dem <- project(dem, "EPSG:4326")
}

bbox <- sf::st_bbox(basemap_wgs84)
ext_cn <- ext(bbox$xmin, bbox$xmax, bbox$ymin, bbox$ymax)

dem_cn <- crop(dem, ext_cn)

# If the raster has >= 3 layers (e.g. grayscale stored as RGB),
# convert it to a single grayscale layer
if (nlyr(dem_cn) >= 3) {
  dem_cn <- (dem_cn[[1]] + dem_cn[[2]] + dem_cn[[3]]) / 3
}

```

## Import, validate and prepare the source data
```{r import-and-validate}
ancient_chi_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
  data_file,
  sheet = "Analysis_Data",
  na = c("", "-", "NA", "N/A"),
  trim_ws = TRUE
)

ancient_chi_all <- ancient_chi_raw %>%
  mutate(
    indiv_id = as.character(indiv_id),
    site_id = as.character(site_id),
    period = factor(period_proposed, levels = PERIOD_CODES)
  )

# Check whether individual identifiers are missing or duplicated
if (anyNA(ancient_chi_all$indiv_id) ||
    anyDuplicated(ancient_chi_all$indiv_id) > 0) {
  stop("There are missing or duplicate individual identifiers; please check `indiv_id`")
}

# Examine site groupings, sex, and periods
if (anyNA(ancient_chi_all$site_id) ||
    anyNA(ancient_chi_all$period) ||
    any(!ancient_chi_all$sex %in% c(0, 1))) {
  stop("Please check site_id, period_proposed, and sex")
}

# Ensure that each site-period group corresponds to only one period
group_period_check <- ancient_chi_all %>%
  distinct(site_id, period) %>%
  count(site_id)

if (any(group_period_check$n > 1)) {
  stop("A single site_id corresponds to multiple time periods; please check the grouping")
}
```

### FBL, brachial index and crural index

Auerbach (2011), AJPA 145:67–80, p. 76,
[doi:10.1002/ajpa.21469](https://doi.org/10.1002/ajpa.21469):
`FBL = 0.995 * FXL - 1.557`, in mm, using the same equation for both sexes.
The original paper calls maximum femoral length FML; this workbook calls it FXL.
```{r fbl-and-indices}
ancient_chi_all <- ancient_chi_all %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    FBL = 0.995 * FXL - 1.557,
    BI = 100 * RXL / HXL,
    CI = 100 * TXL / FBL,
    FBL_source = if_else(is.na(FBL), "missing_no_FXL", "estimated_Auerbach2011")
  )

#  Remove the commingled assemblage SDC
ancient_chi_primary_source <- ancient_chi_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(site_id != "SDC")
ancient_chi_detail_fig2 <- ancient_chi_primary_source

# Check sample size
sample_by_group <- ancient_chi_primary_source %>%
  dplyr::count(site_id, period, sex, name = "N")
readr::write_csv(sample_by_group,
                 file.path(audit_dir, "primary_group_period_sex_counts.csv"))
View(sample_by_group)

# sample size for each trait
sample_by_trait <- ancient_chi_primary_source %>%
  dplyr::group_by(sex) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    FXL = sum(!is.na(FXL)), FBL = sum(!is.na(FBL)),
    FHD = sum(!is.na(FHD)), TXL = sum(!is.na(TXL)),
    HXL = sum(!is.na(HXL)), RXL = sum(!is.na(RXL)),
    BI = sum(!is.na(BI)), CI = sum(!is.na(CI)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(sample_by_trait)
readr::write_csv(sample_by_trait,
                 file.path(audit_dir, "primary_trait_availability.csv"))
View(sample_by_trait)
```

## Extract environmental covariates without silent sample loss
Use the WorldClim 2.1 30-second layers listed in `climate_paths`. Raster
values are retained in their source units, then standardised for modelling.
The workbook's lowercase `altitude` is retained as metadata; the model uses
uppercase `Altitude`, extracted from the elevation raster, as in the original.
```{r environmental-covariates}
#  Check whether the climate file exists.
missing_rasters <- climate_paths[!file.exists(climate_paths)]

if (length(missing_rasters) > 0) {
  print(missing_rasters)
  stop("The above file(s) could not be found; please check the paths in `climate_paths`")
}

# Read in five environmental layers and assign variable names.
climate_rasters <- terra::rast(unname(climate_paths))
names(climate_rasters) <- names(climate_paths)

if (terra::crs(climate_rasters) == "") {
  stop("The environment layer lacks coordinate system information")
}

# Define an extraction function; it will also be used for the subsequent prediction maps
extract_environment <- function(data) {

  # Convert latitude and longitude into points on a map
  points <- terra::vect(
    as.data.frame(data),
    geom = c("longitude", "latitude"),
    crs = "EPSG:4326"
  )

  # Transform the point into the coordinate system of the environment layer
  points <- terra::project(points, terra::crs(climate_rasters))

  # Extract the environmental values ​​for the grid cells in which each point is located
  terra::extract(
    climate_rasters,
    points,
    method = "simple",
    ID = FALSE
  )
}

# Select data for environmental extraction
# SDC is excluded by default; however, when sensitivity analysis is enabled, environmental values are also extracted for SDC (see subsection 11)
extraction_source <- ancient_chi_primary_source

if (run_sdc_sensitivity) {
  extraction_source <- ancient_chi_all
}

#  Check latitude and longitude
invalid_coordinates <- extraction_source %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.finite(longitude) | !is.finite(latitude) |
      longitude < -180 | longitude > 180 |
      latitude < -90 | latitude > 90
  )

if (nrow(invalid_coordinates) > 0) {
  readr::write_csv(
    invalid_coordinates,
    file.path(audit_dir, "invalid_coordinates.csv")
  )
  stop("Some latitude and longitude values are incorrect; please check invalid_coordinates.csv")
}

# Extract environmental values and add them to the original data table.
environment_values <- extract_environment(extraction_source)

extraction_source <- dplyr::bind_cols(
  extraction_source,
  environment_values
)

# Check for any individuals for which extraction failed
environment_gaps <- extraction_source %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.finite(Mintemp) | !is.finite(Maxtemp) |
      !is.finite(Minprecip) | !is.finite(Maxprecip) |
      !is.finite(Altitude)
  )

readr::write_csv(
  environment_gaps,
  file.path(audit_dir, "missing_environment.csv")
)

if (nrow(environment_gaps) > 0) {
  stop("Some individuals lack environmental values; please refer to missing_environment.csv")
}

# Save data containing environment variables
readr::write_csv(
  extraction_source,
  file.path(audit_dir, "data_with_environment.csv")
)

# Record the environment files used this time
climate_file_info <- data.frame(
  variable = names(climate_paths),
  path = unname(climate_paths),
  md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(climate_paths))
)

readr::write_csv(
  climate_file_info,
  file.path(audit_dir, "environmental_file_manifest.csv")
)

#  Prepare data for the main analysis and for gender-specific analyses: the main analysis always excludes SDC, i.e., the commingled remains
ancient_chi_detail <- extraction_source %>%
  dplyr::filter(site_id != "SDC")

ancient_chi_male <- ancient_chi_detail %>%
  dplyr::filter(sex == 0)

ancient_chi_female <- ancient_chi_detail %>%
  dplyr::filter(sex == 1)

# Record the sample size at each stage
sample_all <- ancient_chi_all %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    stage = "source_all",
    N = n(),
    male = sum(sex == 0),
    female = sum(sex == 1),
    site_period_groups = n_distinct(site_id)
  )

sample_primary <- ancient_chi_primary_source %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    stage = "primary_noSDC_source",
    N = n(),
    male = sum(sex == 0),
    female = sum(sex == 1),
    site_period_groups = n_distinct(site_id)
  )

sample_environment <- ancient_chi_detail %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    stage = "primary_noSDC_environment_complete",
    N = n(),
    male = sum(sex == 0),
    female = sum(sex == 1),
    site_period_groups = n_distinct(site_id)
  )

sample_flow <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sample_all,
  sample_primary,
  sample_environment
)

print(sample_flow)

readr::write_csv(
  sample_flow,
  file.path(audit_dir, "sample_flow.csv")
)

```

## Male FXL
### 1. Analysis data and standardisation
```{r male-fxl-data}
male_FXL_exclusions <- ancient_chi_male %>%
  filter(is.na(FXL))
readr::write_csv(male_FXL_exclusions,
                file.path(audit_dir, "male_FXL_missing_trait_or_dates.csv"))

ancient_chi_male_FXL <- ancient_chi_male %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(FXL))

model_variables <- c("longitude", "latitude", "Mintemp", "Maxtemp",
                     "Minprecip", "Maxprecip", "Altitude", "FXL")
if (nrow(ancient_chi_male_FXL) < 2) stop("Insufficient male FXL samples")
stopifnot(!anyNA(ancient_chi_male_FXL$site_id),
          !any(ancient_chi_male_FXL$site_id == "SDC"))

# Pre-standardization check: Must not contain infinite values, nor can there be a zero standard deviation.
for (nm in model_variables) {
  x <- ancient_chi_male_FXL[[nm]]
  if (!is.numeric(x) || any(!is.finite(x)) || sd(x) <= 0) {
    stop("Please check the male FXL model variables:", nm)
  }
}

ancient_chi_male_FXL <- ancient_chi_male_FXL %>%
  mutate(
    longitude_scaled = as.numeric(scale(longitude)),
    latitude_scaled  = as.numeric(scale(latitude)),
    mintemp_scaled   = as.numeric(scale(Mintemp)),
    maxtemp_scaled   = as.numeric(scale(Maxtemp)),
    minprecip_scaled = as.numeric(scale(Minprecip)),
    maxprecip_scaled = as.numeric(scale(Maxprecip)),
    altitude_scaled = as.numeric(scale(Altitude)),
    FXL_z           = as.numeric(scale(FXL))
  )

male_FXL_longitude_center <- mean(ancient_chi_male_FXL$longitude)
male_FXL_longitude_scale  <- sd(ancient_chi_male_FXL$longitude)
male_FXL_latitude_center  <- mean(ancient_chi_male_FXL$latitude)
male_FXL_latitude_scale   <- sd(ancient_chi_male_FXL$latitude)
male_FXL_mintemp_center   <- mean(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Mintemp)
male_FXL_mintemp_scale    <- sd(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Mintemp)
male_FXL_maxtemp_center   <- mean(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Maxtemp)
male_FXL_maxtemp_scale    <- sd(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Maxtemp)
male_FXL_minprecip_center <- mean(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Minprecip)
male_FXL_minprecip_scale  <- sd(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Minprecip)
male_FXL_maxprecip_center <- mean(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Maxprecip)
male_FXL_maxprecip_scale  <- sd(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Maxprecip)
male_FXL_altitude_center  <- mean(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Altitude)
male_FXL_altitude_scale   <- sd(ancient_chi_male_FXL$Altitude)
mean_fxl_male <- mean(ancient_chi_male_FXL$FXL)
sd_fxl_male   <- sd(ancient_chi_male_FXL$FXL)

# Also, save a parameter table to facilitate review and reproduction
male_FXL_scaling <- tibble(
  variable = model_variables,
  center = c(male_FXL_longitude_center, male_FXL_latitude_center,
             male_FXL_mintemp_center, male_FXL_maxtemp_center,
             male_FXL_minprecip_center, male_FXL_maxprecip_center,
             male_FXL_altitude_center, mean_fxl_male),
  scale = c(male_FXL_longitude_scale, male_FXL_latitude_scale,
            male_FXL_mintemp_scale, male_FXL_maxtemp_scale,
            male_FXL_minprecip_scale, male_FXL_maxprecip_scale,
            male_FXL_altitude_scale, sd_fxl_male)
)

# Set the period and site group as categorical variables
male_FXL_main_data <- ancient_chi_male_FXL %>%
  mutate(
    period = droplevels(factor(as.character(period), levels = PERIOD_CODES)),
    site_id = factor(site_id)
  )

levs <- levels(male_FXL_main_data$period)
contrasts(male_FXL_main_data$period) <- contr.sum(length(levs))

sample_model <- male_FXL_main_data %>%
  summarise(stage = "male_FXL_primary_model", N = n(),
            male = sum(sex == 0), female = sum(sex == 1),
            site_period_groups = n_distinct(site_id))

sample_flow <- sample_flow %>% filter(stage != "male_FXL_primary_model")
sample_flow <- bind_rows(sample_flow, sample_model)

readr::write_csv(sample_flow, file.path(audit_dir, "sample_flow.csv")) 
readr::write_csv(male_FXL_scaling,
                file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_primary_scaling.csv")) 
readr::write_csv(male_FXL_main_data,
                file.path(audit_dir, "male_FXL_primary_model_data.csv")) 

print(sample_model) # Final modeling data
print(count(male_FXL_main_data, period, name = "N")) # Sample size for each analysis stage
print(male_FXL_scaling) # Mean and standard deviation used for standardization
```

### 2. Fit the primary model
```{r male-fxl-fit}
priors_common <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sigma"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sd", group = "site_id"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sds"),
  prior(gamma(2, 0.1), class = "nu")
)
male_FXL_formula <- bf(
  FXL_z ~ period + t2(longitude_scaled, latitude_scaled) +
    mintemp_scaled + maxtemp_scaled + minprecip_scaled + maxprecip_scaled +
    altitude_scaled + (1 | site_id)
)
fit_male_FXL_main <- brm(
  formula = male_FXL_formula, data = male_FXL_main_data,
  family = student(), prior = priors_common,
  iter = 4000, warmup = 1000, chains = 4, cores = 4,
  seed = SEED, backend = stan_backend, control = brms_control,
  refresh = 500,
  file = file.path(model_dir, "male_FXL_primary_noSDC"),
  file_refit = refit_mode
)
```

### 3. Model diagnostics
```{r male-fxl-diagnostics}
print(summary(fit_male_FXL_main, prob = 0.90))
writeLines(capture.output(summary(fit_male_FXL_main, prob = 0.90)),
           file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_model_summary.txt"))

male_FXL_diagnostics <- posterior::summarise_draws(
  posterior::as_draws_array(fit_male_FXL_main)
)
nuts_male_FXL <- brms::nuts_params(fit_male_FXL_main)
male_FXL_sampler <- tibble(
  divergences = sum(nuts_male_FXL$Parameter == "divergent__" &
                     nuts_male_FXL$Value > 0),
  max_treedepth_hits = sum(nuts_male_FXL$Parameter == "treedepth__" &
                            nuts_male_FXL$Value >= brms_control$max_treedepth)
)
readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(male_FXL_diagnostics),
                file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_posterior_diagnostics.csv"))
readr::write_csv(male_FXL_sampler,
                file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_sampler_diagnostics.csv"))
print(male_FXL_sampler)
if (any(male_FXL_diagnostics$rhat > 1.01, na.rm = TRUE) ||
    any(male_FXL_diagnostics$ess_bulk < 400, na.rm = TRUE) ||
    any(male_FXL_diagnostics$ess_tail < 400, na.rm = TRUE) ||
    male_FXL_sampler$divergences > 0 || male_FXL_sampler$max_treedepth_hits > 0) {
  warning("Please check model convergence and sampling diagnostics before interpreting the results")
}
set.seed(SEED + 1L)
p_ppc_male_FXL <- pp_check(fit_male_FXL_main, ndraws = 100)
print(p_ppc_male_FXL)
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "male_FXL_posterior_predictive_check.png"),
       p_ppc_male_FXL, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

### 4. Period differences
These are conditional predictions, with latitude, longitude, and environmental variables held constant at their respective means from the modeling sample, and with group-level random intercepts excluded.
The horizontal axis represents ordered time periods; their equidistant spacing does not imply that the durations of these periods are equal. Connecting lines are provided solely to aid readability.
The right-hand axis displays values ​​converted back into millimeters, using the mean and standard deviation of FXL from the same modeling sample.
#### Shared style
```{r temporal-shared-style}
time_plot_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.25),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(l = 8, r = 10)),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(margin = margin(l = 8,r = 8)),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5, lineheight = 0.9
    )
  )
```

```{r male-fxl-period}
ce_time_male_fxl <- conditional_effects(
  fit_male_FXL_main, effects = "period", re_formula = NA,
  method = "posterior_epred", prob = 0.90, robust = TRUE,
  conditions = data.frame(
    longitude_scaled = 0, latitude_scaled = 0,
    mintemp_scaled = 0, maxtemp_scaled = 0,
    minprecip_scaled = 0, maxprecip_scaled = 0, altitude_scaled = 0
  )
)
ce_df_male_FXL <- as.data.frame(ce_time_male_fxl$period) %>%
  mutate(
    period_num = match(as.character(period), PERIOD_CODES),
    median_mm = mean_fxl_male + estimate__ * sd_fxl_male,
    lower90_mm = mean_fxl_male + lower__ * sd_fxl_male,
    upper90_mm = mean_fxl_male + upper__ * sd_fxl_male
  ) %>% arrange(period_num)
male_FXL_z_breaks <- c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2)
readr::write_csv(ce_df_male_FXL, file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_temporal_median_CI90.csv"))

p_time_male_fxl <- ggplot(
  ce_df_male_FXL, aes(x = period_num, y = estimate__)
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__),
    fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.45
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.95) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(PERIOD_CODES), labels = PERIOD_PLOT_LABELS
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Predicted FXL (z-score)",
    breaks = male_FXL_z_breaks,
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      transform = ~ mean_fxl_male + . * sd_fxl_male,
      breaks = mean_fxl_male + male_FXL_z_breaks * sd_fxl_male,
      labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
      name = "Predicted FXL (mm)"
    )
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, title = "Male") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-2, 2)) +
  time_plot_theme

print(p_time_male_fxl)
```



### 5. Environmental fixed effects

Calculate the median and the 5%/95% quantiles directly from the same set of posterior draws to serve as plotting points and intervals.
These coefficients represent conditional associations—accounting for other variables—and do not automatically imply causal effects.

```{r male-fxl-fixed}
fixef_long_male_fxl <- fit_male_FXL_main %>%
  tidybayes::gather_draws(b_mintemp_scaled, b_maxtemp_scaled,
                        b_minprecip_scaled, b_maxprecip_scaled, b_altitude_scaled) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(parameter = factor(
    .variable,
    levels = c("b_mintemp_scaled", "b_maxtemp_scaled", "b_minprecip_scaled",
               "b_maxprecip_scaled", "b_altitude_scaled"),
    labels = c("Min temp", "Max temp", "Min precip", "Max precip", "Altitude")
  ))
fixed_effect_summary <- fixef_long_male_fxl %>%
  group_by(parameter) %>%
  summarise(median = median(.value), lower90 = quantile(.value, 0.05),
            upper90 = quantile(.value, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
readr::write_csv(fixed_effect_summary,
                file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_environmental_effects_median_CI90.csv"))

p_fixed_male_fxl <- ggplot(fixef_long_male_fxl, aes(.value, parameter)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.7) +
  tidybayes::stat_halfeye(point_interval = NULL, fill = "skyblue",
                         alpha = 0.65, slab_colour = NA) +
  geom_segment(data = fixed_effect_summary,
               aes(x = lower90, xend = upper90, y = parameter, yend = parameter),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = fixed_effect_summary, aes(x = median, y = parameter),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.5) +
  labs(title = "Male", x = NULL, y = "FXL") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),    
        axis.text= element_text(size = 11),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))
print(p_fixed_male_fxl)
```

### 6. Site-period group random intercepts
Candidate groups comprise the 15 lowest and 15 highest posterior median random intercepts and any groups whose 90% credible intervals exclude zero. Display at most 60 groups, prioritising those with the largest absolute posterior medians. Save the full results to CSV.

```{r male-fxl-random}
site_re_male_FXL <- fit_male_FXL_main %>%
  tidybayes::spread_draws(r_site_id[site_id, Intercept]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(site_id = as.character(site_id), r_site_id = as.numeric(r_site_id))
site_qi90_male_FXL <- site_re_male_FXL %>%
  group_by(site_id) %>%
  summarise(median = median(r_site_id), lower90 = quantile(r_site_id, 0.05),
            upper90 = quantile(r_site_id, 0.95), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(deviated_90 = lower90 > 0 | upper90 < 0) %>% arrange(median)
keep_sites_male_FXL <- union(
  c(head(site_qi90_male_FXL$site_id, 15), tail(site_qi90_male_FXL$site_id, 15)),
  site_qi90_male_FXL$site_id[site_qi90_male_FXL$deviated_90]
)
site_qi_plot <- site_qi90_male_FXL %>%
  filter(site_id %in% keep_sites_male_FXL) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(median))) %>% slice_head(n = 60) %>% arrange(median)
site_levels_male_FXL <- site_qi_plot$site_id
site_qi_plot$site_id <- factor(site_qi_plot$site_id, levels = site_levels_male_FXL)
site_re_plot_male_FXL <- site_re_male_FXL %>%
  filter(site_id %in% site_levels_male_FXL) %>%
  mutate(site_id = factor(site_id, levels = site_levels_male_FXL))
site_qi90_male_FXL <- site_qi90_male_FXL %>%
  mutate(shown_in_plot = site_id %in% site_levels_male_FXL)
readr::write_csv(site_qi90_male_FXL,
                file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_all_group_intercepts_median_CI90.csv"))

p_random_male_FXL <- ggplot(site_re_plot_male_FXL, aes(r_site_id, site_id)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey35") +
  tidybayes::stat_halfeye(point_interval = NULL, height = 0.55,
                         slab_colour = NA, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_segment(data = site_qi_plot,
               aes(x = lower90, xend = upper90, y = site_id, yend = site_id),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_point(data = site_qi_plot, aes(x = median, y = site_id),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.1) +
  labs(x = "Group random intercept (z-score)", y = "Site-period groups", title = "Male") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
print(p_random_male_FXL)
```

### 7. Spatial prediction grid
```{r male-fxl-grid}
sites_all <- male_FXL_main_data %>% distinct(site_id, longitude, latitude)
site_points <- sf::st_as_sf(sites_all, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)
hull_all <- site_points %>% sf::st_transform(3857) %>%
  sf::st_union() %>% sf::st_convex_hull() %>%
  sf::st_buffer(dist = if (nrow(sites_all) < 3) 30000 else 20000) %>%
  sf::st_transform(4326) %>% sf::st_make_valid()

grid_geo <- expand.grid(
  Longitude = seq(70, 140, length.out = grid_resolution),
  Latitude  = seq(10, 60, length.out = grid_resolution)
) %>% as_tibble()
grid_points <- sf::st_as_sf(grid_geo, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326)
inside <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(grid_points, hull_all)) > 0
grid_geo <- grid_geo[inside, , drop = FALSE]
if (!nrow(grid_geo)) stop("There are no grid points within the prediction mask.")

# Use the existing `terra` environment layer directly
grid_vector <- terra::vect(as.data.frame(grid_geo),
                           geom = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
grid_vector <- terra::project(grid_vector, terra::crs(climate_rasters))
grid_environment <- terra::extract(climate_rasters, grid_vector,
                                   method = "simple", ID = FALSE)
grid_scaled_base <- bind_cols(grid_geo, grid_environment)
grid_gaps <- grid_scaled_base %>%
  filter(!if_all(all_of(names(climate_paths)), is.finite))
readr::write_csv(grid_gaps, file.path(audit_dir, "grid_cells_without_environment.csv"))
message("Number of prediction grid points excluded due to missing environmental values:", nrow(grid_gaps))

grid_scaled_base <- grid_scaled_base %>%
  filter(if_all(all_of(names(climate_paths)), is.finite)) %>%
  mutate(
    longitude_scaled = (Longitude - male_FXL_longitude_center) / male_FXL_longitude_scale,
    latitude_scaled  = (Latitude - male_FXL_latitude_center) / male_FXL_latitude_scale,
    mintemp_scaled   = (Mintemp - male_FXL_mintemp_center) / male_FXL_mintemp_scale,
    maxtemp_scaled   = (Maxtemp - male_FXL_maxtemp_center) / male_FXL_maxtemp_scale,
    minprecip_scaled = (Minprecip - male_FXL_minprecip_center) / male_FXL_minprecip_scale,
    maxprecip_scaled = (Maxprecip - male_FXL_maxprecip_center) / male_FXL_maxprecip_scale,
    altitude_scaled = (Altitude - male_FXL_altitude_center) / male_FXL_altitude_scale
  )
if (!nrow(grid_scaled_base)) stop("A prediction grid lacking complete environmental values")
```


### 8. Chunked prediction and averaging across periods

In each instance, `posterior_epred()` returns a matrix with dimensions "number of draws × number of grid points."
The same set of `draw_ids` is used across all time periods and batches. For each draw, the predictions are first averaged across time periods (with equal weighting),
after which the median and the 5th/95th percentiles of these averaged predictions are calculated.
The resulting intervals reflect the uncertainty surrounding the expected FXL.

Here, two explicit loops are maintained: an outer loop that processes the grid in batches, and an inner loop that generates predictions for each time period.

Batching helps limit the size of the prediction matrix, preventing the need to expand the entire grid and all time periods simultaneously.

```{r male-fxl-predictions}
levs <- levels(male_FXL_main_data$period)
period_contrasts <- contrasts(male_FXL_main_data$period)
n_available_draws <- posterior::ndraws(posterior::as_draws_array(fit_male_FXL_main))
set.seed(SEED + 100L)
draw_ids <- seq_len(n_available_draws)
if (!is.null(prediction_ndraws)) {
  draw_ids <- sort(sample.int(n_available_draws,
                             min(prediction_ndraws, n_available_draws)))
}
readr::write_csv(tibble(draw_id = draw_ids),
                file.path(audit_dir, "male_FXL_spatial_draw_ids.csv"))

grid_segments <- split(seq_len(nrow(grid_scaled_base)),
                        ceiling(seq_len(nrow(grid_scaled_base)) / prediction_chunk_cells))
all_period_chunks <- vector("list", length(grid_segments))
period_chunks <- vector("list", length(grid_segments))

for (j in seq_along(grid_segments)) {
  message("Predicting chunk ", j, " / ", length(grid_segments))
  chunk <- grid_scaled_base[grid_segments[[j]], , drop = FALSE]
  mean_draws <- matrix(0, nrow = length(draw_ids), ncol = nrow(chunk))
  period_results <- vector("list", length(levs))

  for (k in seq_along(levs)) {
    newdata <- chunk
    newdata$period <- factor(rep(levs[k], nrow(chunk)), levels = levs)
    contrasts(newdata$period) <- period_contrasts
    newdata$site_id <- factor(rep(levels(male_FXL_main_data$site_id)[1], nrow(chunk)),
                              levels = levels(male_FXL_main_data$site_id))
    # `site_id` provides a valid level; `re_formula = NA` excludes its random intercept.
    ep <- brms::posterior_epred(fit_male_FXL_main, newdata = newdata,
                                re_formula = NA, draw_ids = draw_ids)
    stopifnot(is.matrix(ep), nrow(ep) == length(draw_ids),
              ncol(ep) == nrow(chunk), all(is.finite(ep)))

    # Average predictions across periods with equal weights within each posterior draw
    mean_draws <- mean_draws + ep / length(levs)
    q_period <- apply(ep, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
    period_results[[k]] <- tibble(
      Longitude = chunk$Longitude, Latitude = chunk$Latitude,
      period = levs[k], period_num = match(levs[k], PERIOD_CODES),
      male_FXL_epred_median = q_period[2, ],
      male_FXL_epred_lower90 = q_period[1, ],
      male_FXL_epred_upper90 = q_period[3, ]
    )
  }

  q_all <- apply(mean_draws, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
  all_period_chunks[[j]] <- tibble(
    Longitude = chunk$Longitude, Latitude = chunk$Latitude,
    med = q_all[2, ], low = q_all[1, ], high = q_all[3, ],
    period_all = "All represented periods (equal weights)"
  )
  period_chunks[[j]] <- bind_rows(period_results)
}

pred_all_masked <- bind_rows(all_period_chunks)
male_FXL_grid_7periods <- bind_rows(period_chunks)
# Retain the original object names; the actual number of rows is determined by the number of periods for which there are samples in the model
readr::write_csv(pred_all_masked,
                file.path(out_dir, "male_FXL_grid_all_periods_draw_average_CI90.csv"))
readr::write_csv(male_FXL_grid_7periods,
                file.path(out_dir, "male_FXL_grid_epred_primary_noSDC_median_CI90.csv"))
```

### 11. Optional sensitivity model including SDC commingled remains

By default, `run_sdc_sensitivity = FALSE`, so this section is not executed.
To perform a comparison, first change this to `TRUE` in the Setup phase, **re-run the environment extraction code**, and then proceed with the subsequent steps.
This section only adds models that incorporate SDC commingled remains; it does not alter the primary model objects. It utilizes the standardized parameters from the main analysis.
This represents a single-item sensitivity analysis for males (FXL) and does not constitute a comprehensive sensitivity analysis covering all genders and traits.

```{r male-fxl-sensitivity}
if (run_sdc_sensitivity) {
  male_FXL_withSDC_data <- extraction_source %>%
    filter(sex == 0, !is.na(FXL)) %>%
    mutate(
      longitude_scaled = (longitude - male_FXL_longitude_center) / male_FXL_longitude_scale,
      latitude_scaled  = (latitude - male_FXL_latitude_center) / male_FXL_latitude_scale,
      mintemp_scaled   = (Mintemp - male_FXL_mintemp_center) / male_FXL_mintemp_scale,
      maxtemp_scaled   = (Maxtemp - male_FXL_maxtemp_center) / male_FXL_maxtemp_scale,
      minprecip_scaled = (Minprecip - male_FXL_minprecip_center) / male_FXL_minprecip_scale,
      maxprecip_scaled = (Maxprecip - male_FXL_maxprecip_center) / male_FXL_maxprecip_scale,
      altitude_scaled = (Altitude - male_FXL_altitude_center) / male_FXL_altitude_scale,
      FXL_z = (FXL - mean_fxl_male) / sd_fxl_male,
      period = factor(as.character(period), levels = levs), site_id = factor(site_id)
    )
  if (!any(male_FXL_withSDC_data$site_id == "SDC")) {
    stop("There are no SDC individuals available in the data containing SDC; please check whether the environment extraction needs to be re-run")
  }
  if (anyNA(male_FXL_withSDC_data$period)) {
    stop("SDC introduces time periods not included in the primary analysis; therefore, the comparison design must first be examined")
  }
  contrasts(male_FXL_withSDC_data$period) <- contrasts(male_FXL_main_data$period)
  fit_male_FXL_withSDC <- brm(
    formula = male_FXL_formula, data = male_FXL_withSDC_data,
    family = student(), prior = priors_common,
    iter = 4000, warmup = 1000, chains = 4, cores = 4,
    seed = SEED + 10L, backend = stan_backend, control = brms_control, refresh = 500,
    file = file.path(model_dir, "male_FXL_sensitivity_withSDC"), file_refit = refit_mode
  )
  print(summary(fit_male_FXL_withSDC, prob = 0.90))
  sensitivity_diagnostics <- posterior::summarise_draws(
    posterior::as_draws_array(fit_male_FXL_withSDC)
  )
  sensitivity_nuts <- brms::nuts_params(fit_male_FXL_withSDC)
  sensitivity_sampler <- tibble(
    divergences = sum(sensitivity_nuts$Parameter == "divergent__" & sensitivity_nuts$Value > 0),
    max_treedepth_hits = sum(sensitivity_nuts$Parameter == "treedepth__" &
                              sensitivity_nuts$Value >= brms_control$max_treedepth)
  )
  print(sensitivity_sampler)
  if (any(sensitivity_diagnostics$rhat > 1.01, na.rm = TRUE) ||
      any(sensitivity_diagnostics$ess_bulk < 400, na.rm = TRUE) ||
      any(sensitivity_diagnostics$ess_tail < 400, na.rm = TRUE) ||
      sensitivity_sampler$divergences > 0 || sensitivity_sampler$max_treedepth_hits > 0) {
    warning("Convergence or sampling diagnostics for models involving SDC need to be checked")
  }
  readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(sensitivity_diagnostics),
                  file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_withSDC_diagnostics.csv"))
  readr::write_csv(sensitivity_sampler,
                  file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_withSDC_sampler.csv"))
  main_fixed <- as.data.frame(fixef(fit_male_FXL_main, robust = TRUE, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))) %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>% mutate(model = "primary_noSDC")
  sensitivity_fixed <- as.data.frame(fixef(fit_male_FXL_withSDC, robust = TRUE, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))) %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>% mutate(model = "sensitivity_withSDC")
  readr::write_csv(bind_rows(main_fixed, sensitivity_fixed),
                  file.path(table_dir, "male_FXL_SDC_fixed_effects_comparison.csv"))
}
```


## Female FXL

Female z-scores are based on the female FXL analysis sample. Identical z-scores for males and females do not correspond to the same length in millimeters;
when comparing absolute lengths, the respective means and standard deviations should be used for back-transformation.
The spatial intervals reflect the uncertainty in the expected mean FXL over time, rather than serving as prediction intervals for individual observations.

```{r female-fxl-settings}
female_FXL_seed <- SEED + 1000L
```

### 1. Analysis data and standardisation

```{r female-fxl-data}
female_FXL_exclusions <- ancient_chi_female %>%
  filter(is.na(FXL) )
readr::write_csv(female_FXL_exclusions,
                file.path(audit_dir, "female_FXL_missing_trait_or_dates.csv"))

ancient_chi_female_FXL <- ancient_chi_female %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.na(FXL))

female_FXL_model_variables <- c("longitude", "latitude", "Mintemp", "Maxtemp",
                     "Minprecip", "Maxprecip", "Altitude", "FXL")
if (nrow(ancient_chi_female_FXL) < 2) stop("Lack female fxl samples")
stopifnot(all(ancient_chi_female_FXL$sex == 1),
          !anyNA(ancient_chi_female_FXL$site_id),
          !any(ancient_chi_female_FXL$site_id == "SDC"))

for (female_FXL_variable in female_FXL_model_variables) {
  female_FXL_values <- ancient_chi_female_FXL[[female_FXL_variable]]
  if (!is.numeric(female_FXL_values) || any(!is.finite(female_FXL_values)) || sd(female_FXL_values) <= 0) {
    stop("Please check the female FXL model variables:", female_FXL_variable)
  }
}

ancient_chi_female_FXL <- ancient_chi_female_FXL %>%
  mutate(
    longitude_scaled = as.numeric(scale(longitude)),
    latitude_scaled  = as.numeric(scale(latitude)),
    mintemp_scaled   = as.numeric(scale(Mintemp)),
    maxtemp_scaled   = as.numeric(scale(Maxtemp)),
    minprecip_scaled = as.numeric(scale(Minprecip)),
    maxprecip_scaled = as.numeric(scale(Maxprecip)),
    altitude_scaled = as.numeric(scale(Altitude)),
    FXL_z           = as.numeric(scale(FXL))
  )

female_FXL_longitude_center <- mean(ancient_chi_female_FXL$longitude)
female_FXL_longitude_scale  <- sd(ancient_chi_female_FXL$longitude)
female_FXL_latitude_center  <- mean(ancient_chi_female_FXL$latitude)
female_FXL_latitude_scale   <- sd(ancient_chi_female_FXL$latitude)
female_FXL_mintemp_center   <- mean(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Mintemp)
female_FXL_mintemp_scale    <- sd(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Mintemp)
female_FXL_maxtemp_center   <- mean(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Maxtemp)
female_FXL_maxtemp_scale    <- sd(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Maxtemp)
female_FXL_minprecip_center <- mean(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Minprecip)
female_FXL_minprecip_scale  <- sd(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Minprecip)
female_FXL_maxprecip_center <- mean(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Maxprecip)
female_FXL_maxprecip_scale  <- sd(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Maxprecip)
female_FXL_altitude_center  <- mean(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Altitude)
female_FXL_altitude_scale   <- sd(ancient_chi_female_FXL$Altitude)
mean_fxl_female <- mean(ancient_chi_female_FXL$FXL)
sd_fxl_female   <- sd(ancient_chi_female_FXL$FXL)

# Also, save a parameter table to facilitate review and reproduction
female_FXL_scaling <- tibble(
  variable = female_FXL_model_variables,
  center = c(female_FXL_longitude_center, female_FXL_latitude_center,
             female_FXL_mintemp_center, female_FXL_maxtemp_center,
             female_FXL_minprecip_center, female_FXL_maxprecip_center,
             female_FXL_altitude_center, mean_fxl_female),
  scale = c(female_FXL_longitude_scale, female_FXL_latitude_scale,
            female_FXL_mintemp_scale, female_FXL_maxtemp_scale,
            female_FXL_minprecip_scale, female_FXL_maxprecip_scale,
            female_FXL_altitude_scale, sd_fxl_female)
)

# Set the period and site group as categorical variables
female_FXL_main_data <- ancient_chi_female_FXL %>%
  mutate(
    period = droplevels(factor(as.character(period), levels = PERIOD_CODES)),
    site_id = factor(site_id)
  )

female_FXL_period_levels <- levels(female_FXL_main_data$period)
if (length(female_FXL_period_levels) < 2) {
  stop("At least two periods with observed data are required for the female FXL model")
}
contrasts(female_FXL_main_data$period) <- contr.sum(length(female_FXL_period_levels))

female_FXL_sample_model <- female_FXL_main_data %>%
  summarise(stage = "female_FXL_primary_model", N = n(),
            male = sum(sex == 0), female = sum(sex == 1),
            site_period_groups = n_distinct(site_id))

sample_flow <- sample_flow %>% filter(stage != "female_FXL_primary_model")
sample_flow <- bind_rows(sample_flow, female_FXL_sample_model)

readr::write_csv(sample_flow, file.path(audit_dir, "sample_flow.csv")) 
readr::write_csv(female_FXL_scaling,
                file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_primary_scaling.csv")) 
readr::write_csv(female_FXL_main_data,
                file.path(audit_dir, "female_FXL_primary_model_data.csv")) 

print(female_FXL_sample_model)
print(count(female_FXL_main_data, period, name = "N"))
print(female_FXL_scaling) 
```

### 2. Fit the primary model

```{r female-fxl-fit}
female_FXL_priors <- c(
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "Intercept"),
  prior(normal(0, 1), class = "b"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sigma"),
  prior(student_t(3, 0, 1), class = "sd", group = "site_id"),
  prior(exponential(1), class = "sds"),
  prior(gamma(2, 0.1), class = "nu")
)
female_FXL_formula <- bf(
  FXL_z ~ period + t2(longitude_scaled, latitude_scaled) +
    mintemp_scaled + maxtemp_scaled + minprecip_scaled + maxprecip_scaled +
    altitude_scaled + (1 | site_id)
)
fit_female_FXL_main <- brm(
  formula = female_FXL_formula, data = female_FXL_main_data,
  family = student(), prior = female_FXL_priors,
  iter = 4000, warmup = 1000, chains = 4, cores = 4,
  seed = female_FXL_seed, backend = stan_backend, control = brms_control,
  refresh = 500,
  file = file.path(model_dir, "female_FXL_primary_noSDC"),
  file_refit = refit_mode
)

# Verify that the model uses all individuals in the prepared analysis sample
stopifnot(nobs(fit_female_FXL_main) == nrow(female_FXL_main_data))
```

### 3. Model diagnostics

```{r female-fxl-diagnostics}
print(summary(fit_female_FXL_main, prob = 0.90))
writeLines(capture.output(summary(fit_female_FXL_main, prob = 0.90)),
           file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_model_summary.txt"))

female_FXL_diagnostics <- posterior::summarise_draws(
  posterior::as_draws_array(fit_female_FXL_main)
)
nuts_female_FXL <- brms::nuts_params(fit_female_FXL_main)
female_FXL_sampler <- tibble(
  divergences = sum(nuts_female_FXL$Parameter == "divergent__" &
                     nuts_female_FXL$Value > 0),
  max_treedepth_hits = sum(nuts_female_FXL$Parameter == "treedepth__" &
                            nuts_female_FXL$Value >= brms_control$max_treedepth)
)
readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(female_FXL_diagnostics),
                file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_posterior_diagnostics.csv"))
readr::write_csv(female_FXL_sampler,
                file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_sampler_diagnostics.csv"))
print(female_FXL_sampler)
if (any(female_FXL_diagnostics$rhat > 1.01, na.rm = TRUE) ||
    any(female_FXL_diagnostics$ess_bulk < 400, na.rm = TRUE) ||
    any(female_FXL_diagnostics$ess_tail < 400, na.rm = TRUE) ||
    female_FXL_sampler$divergences > 0 || female_FXL_sampler$max_treedepth_hits > 0) {
  warning("Check model convergence and sampler diagnostics before interpreting the results")
}
set.seed(female_FXL_seed + 1L)
p_ppc_female_FXL <- pp_check(fit_female_FXL_main, ndraws = 100)
print(p_ppc_female_FXL)
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "female_FXL_posterior_predictive_check.png"),
       p_ppc_female_FXL, width = 7, height = 4.5, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

### 4. Period differences
Fix environmental covariates and coordinates at their means in the female analysis sample and exclude site random intercepts. The secondary axis converts z-scores to millimetres using the female FXL mean and standard deviation.

```{r female-fxl-period}
ce_time_female_fxl <- conditional_effects(
  fit_female_FXL_main, effects = "period", re_formula = NA,
  method = "posterior_epred", prob = 0.90, robust = TRUE,
  conditions = data.frame(
    longitude_scaled = 0, latitude_scaled = 0,
    mintemp_scaled = 0, maxtemp_scaled = 0,
    minprecip_scaled = 0, maxprecip_scaled = 0, altitude_scaled = 0
  )
)
ce_df_female_FXL <- as.data.frame(ce_time_female_fxl$period) %>%
  mutate(
    period_num = match(as.character(period), PERIOD_CODES),
    median_mm = mean_fxl_female + estimate__ * sd_fxl_female,
    lower90_mm = mean_fxl_female + lower__ * sd_fxl_female,
    upper90_mm = mean_fxl_female + upper__ * sd_fxl_female
  ) %>% arrange(period_num)
female_FXL_z_breaks <- c(-2, -1, 0, 1, 2)
readr::write_csv(ce_df_female_FXL, file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_temporal_median_CI90.csv"))

p_time_female_fxl <- ggplot(
  ce_df_female_FXL, aes(x = period_num, y = estimate__)
) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = lower__, ymax = upper__),
    fill = "grey70", alpha = 0.45
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), linewidth = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.95) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_along(PERIOD_CODES), labels = PERIOD_PLOT_LABELS
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Predicted FXL (z-score)",
    breaks = female_FXL_z_breaks,
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      transform = ~ mean_fxl_female + . * sd_fxl_female,
      breaks = mean_fxl_female + female_FXL_z_breaks * sd_fxl_female,
      labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
      name = "Predicted FXL (mm)"
    )
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, title = "Female") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-2, 2)) +
  time_plot_theme

print(p_time_female_fxl)
```

### 5. Environmental fixed effects

Points and line segments indicate posterior medians and 90% credible intervals, respectively

```{r female-fxl-fixed}
fixef_long_female_fxl <- fit_female_FXL_main %>%
  tidybayes::gather_draws(b_mintemp_scaled, b_maxtemp_scaled,
                        b_minprecip_scaled, b_maxprecip_scaled, b_altitude_scaled) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(parameter = factor(
    .variable,
    levels = c("b_mintemp_scaled", "b_maxtemp_scaled", "b_minprecip_scaled",
               "b_maxprecip_scaled", "b_altitude_scaled"),
    labels = c("Min temp", "Max temp", "Min precip", "Max precip", "Altitude")
  ))
female_FXL_fixed_effect_summary <- fixef_long_female_fxl %>%
  group_by(parameter) %>%
  summarise(median = median(.value), lower90 = quantile(.value, 0.05),
            upper90 = quantile(.value, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
readr::write_csv(female_FXL_fixed_effect_summary,
                file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_environmental_effects_median_CI90.csv"))

p_fixed_female_fxl <- ggplot(fixef_long_female_fxl, aes(.value, parameter)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.7) +
  tidybayes::stat_halfeye(point_interval = NULL, fill = "skyblue",
                         alpha = 0.65, slab_colour = NA) +
  geom_segment(data = female_FXL_fixed_effect_summary,
               aes(x = lower90, xend = upper90, y = parameter, yend = parameter),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = female_FXL_fixed_effect_summary, aes(x = median, y = parameter),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.5) +
  labs(title = "Female", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text= element_text(size = 11),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
print(p_fixed_female_fxl)
```

### 6. Site-period group random intercepts

Candidate groups comprise the 15 lowest and 15 highest posterior median random intercepts and any groups whose 90% credible intervals exclude zero. Display at most 60 groups, prioritising those with the largest absolute posterior medians. Save the full results to CSV

```{r female-fxl-random}
site_re_female_FXL <- fit_female_FXL_main %>%
  tidybayes::spread_draws(r_site_id[site_id, Intercept]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(site_id = as.character(site_id), r_site_id = as.numeric(r_site_id))
site_qi90_female_FXL <- site_re_female_FXL %>%
  group_by(site_id) %>%
  summarise(median = median(r_site_id), lower90 = quantile(r_site_id, 0.05),
            upper90 = quantile(r_site_id, 0.95), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(deviated_90 = lower90 > 0 | upper90 < 0) %>% arrange(median)
keep_sites_female_FXL <- union(
  c(head(site_qi90_female_FXL$site_id, 15), tail(site_qi90_female_FXL$site_id, 15)),
  site_qi90_female_FXL$site_id[site_qi90_female_FXL$deviated_90]
)
female_FXL_site_qi_plot <- site_qi90_female_FXL %>%
  filter(site_id %in% keep_sites_female_FXL) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(median))) %>% slice_head(n = 60) %>% arrange(median)
site_levels_female_FXL <- female_FXL_site_qi_plot$site_id
female_FXL_site_qi_plot$site_id <- factor(female_FXL_site_qi_plot$site_id, levels = site_levels_female_FXL)
site_re_plot_female_FXL <- site_re_female_FXL %>%
  filter(site_id %in% site_levels_female_FXL) %>%
  mutate(site_id = factor(site_id, levels = site_levels_female_FXL))
site_qi90_female_FXL <- site_qi90_female_FXL %>%
  mutate(shown_in_plot = site_id %in% site_levels_female_FXL)
readr::write_csv(site_qi90_female_FXL,
                file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_all_group_intercepts_median_CI90.csv"))

p_random_female_FXL <- ggplot(site_re_plot_female_FXL, aes(r_site_id, site_id)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey35") +
  tidybayes::stat_halfeye(point_interval = NULL, height = 0.55,
                         slab_colour = NA, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_segment(data = female_FXL_site_qi_plot,
               aes(x = lower90, xend = upper90, y = site_id, yend = site_id),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_point(data = female_FXL_site_qi_plot, aes(x = median, y = site_id),
             inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 1.1) +
  labs(x = "Group random intercept (z-score)", y = NULL, title = "Female") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
print(p_random_female_FXL)
```

### 7. Spatial prediction grid
Use the geographic extent of sites represented in the female analysis sample. Use the same grid resolution, buffering procedure, and environmental extraction method as in the male analysis.

```{r female-fxl-grid}
female_FXL_sites <- female_FXL_main_data %>% distinct(site_id, longitude, latitude)
female_FXL_site_points <- sf::st_as_sf(female_FXL_sites, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326)
female_FXL_hull <- female_FXL_site_points %>% sf::st_transform(3857) %>%
  sf::st_union() %>% sf::st_convex_hull() %>%
  sf::st_buffer(dist = if (nrow(female_FXL_sites) < 3) 30000 else 20000) %>%
  sf::st_transform(4326) %>% sf::st_make_valid()

female_FXL_grid_geo <- expand.grid(
  Longitude = seq(70, 140, length.out = grid_resolution),
  Latitude  = seq(10, 60, length.out = grid_resolution)
) %>% as_tibble()
female_FXL_grid_points <- sf::st_as_sf(female_FXL_grid_geo, coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = 4326)
female_FXL_inside <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(female_FXL_grid_points, female_FXL_hull)) > 0
female_FXL_grid_geo <- female_FXL_grid_geo[female_FXL_inside, , drop = FALSE]
if (!nrow(female_FXL_grid_geo)) stop("There are no grid points within the prediction mask.")

# Use the existing `terra` environment layer directly
female_FXL_grid_vector <- terra::vect(as.data.frame(female_FXL_grid_geo),
                           geom = c("Longitude", "Latitude"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
female_FXL_grid_vector <- terra::project(female_FXL_grid_vector, terra::crs(climate_rasters))
female_FXL_grid_environment <- terra::extract(climate_rasters, female_FXL_grid_vector,
                                   method = "simple", ID = FALSE)
female_FXL_grid_scaled_base <- bind_cols(female_FXL_grid_geo, female_FXL_grid_environment)
female_FXL_grid_gaps <- female_FXL_grid_scaled_base %>%
  filter(!if_all(all_of(names(climate_paths)), is.finite))
readr::write_csv(female_FXL_grid_gaps, file.path(audit_dir, "female_FXL_grid_cells_without_environment.csv"))
message("Number of prediction grid points excluded due to missing environmental values:", nrow(female_FXL_grid_gaps))

female_FXL_grid_scaled_base <- female_FXL_grid_scaled_base %>%
  filter(if_all(all_of(names(climate_paths)), is.finite)) %>%
  mutate(
    longitude_scaled = (Longitude - female_FXL_longitude_center) / female_FXL_longitude_scale,
    latitude_scaled  = (Latitude - female_FXL_latitude_center) / female_FXL_latitude_scale,
    mintemp_scaled   = (Mintemp - female_FXL_mintemp_center) / female_FXL_mintemp_scale,
    maxtemp_scaled   = (Maxtemp - female_FXL_maxtemp_center) / female_FXL_maxtemp_scale,
    minprecip_scaled = (Minprecip - female_FXL_minprecip_center) / female_FXL_minprecip_scale,
    maxprecip_scaled = (Maxprecip - female_FXL_maxprecip_center) / female_FXL_maxprecip_scale,
    altitude_scaled = (Altitude - female_FXL_altitude_center) / female_FXL_altitude_scale
  )
if (!nrow(female_FXL_grid_scaled_base)) stop("A prediction grid lacking complete environmental values")
```

### 8. Chunked prediction and averaging across periods

```{r female-fxl-predictions}
female_FXL_period_levels <- levels(female_FXL_main_data$period)
female_FXL_period_contrasts <- contrasts(female_FXL_main_data$period)
female_FXL_n_available_draws <- posterior::ndraws(posterior::as_draws_array(fit_female_FXL_main))
set.seed(female_FXL_seed + 100L)
female_FXL_draw_ids <- seq_len(female_FXL_n_available_draws)
if (!is.null(prediction_ndraws)) {
  female_FXL_draw_ids <- sort(sample.int(female_FXL_n_available_draws,
                             min(prediction_ndraws, female_FXL_n_available_draws)))
}
readr::write_csv(tibble(draw_id = female_FXL_draw_ids),
                file.path(audit_dir, "female_FXL_spatial_draw_ids.csv"))

female_FXL_grid_segments <- split(seq_len(nrow(female_FXL_grid_scaled_base)),
                        ceiling(seq_len(nrow(female_FXL_grid_scaled_base)) / prediction_chunk_cells))
female_FXL_all_period_chunks <- vector("list", length(female_FXL_grid_segments))
female_FXL_period_chunks <- vector("list", length(female_FXL_grid_segments))

for (female_FXL_j in seq_along(female_FXL_grid_segments)) {
  message("Female FXL: predicting chunk ", female_FXL_j, " / ", length(female_FXL_grid_segments))
  female_FXL_chunk <- female_FXL_grid_scaled_base[female_FXL_grid_segments[[female_FXL_j]], , drop = FALSE]
  female_FXL_mean_draws <- matrix(0, nrow = length(female_FXL_draw_ids), ncol = nrow(female_FXL_chunk))
  female_FXL_period_results <- vector("list", length(female_FXL_period_levels))

  for (female_FXL_k in seq_along(female_FXL_period_levels)) {
    female_FXL_newdata <- female_FXL_chunk
    female_FXL_newdata$period <- factor(rep(female_FXL_period_levels[female_FXL_k], nrow(female_FXL_chunk)), levels = female_FXL_period_levels)
    contrasts(female_FXL_newdata$period) <- female_FXL_period_contrasts
    female_FXL_newdata$site_id <- factor(rep(levels(female_FXL_main_data$site_id)[1], nrow(female_FXL_chunk)),
                              levels = levels(female_FXL_main_data$site_id))
    # `site_id` provides a valid level; `re_formula = NA` excludes its random intercept.
    female_FXL_ep <- brms::posterior_epred(fit_female_FXL_main, newdata = female_FXL_newdata,
                                re_formula = NA, draw_ids = female_FXL_draw_ids)
    stopifnot(is.matrix(female_FXL_ep), nrow(female_FXL_ep) == length(female_FXL_draw_ids),
              ncol(female_FXL_ep) == nrow(female_FXL_chunk), all(is.finite(female_FXL_ep)))

    # Average predictions across periods with equal weights within each posterior draw
    female_FXL_mean_draws <- female_FXL_mean_draws + female_FXL_ep / length(female_FXL_period_levels)
    female_FXL_q_period <- apply(female_FXL_ep, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
    female_FXL_period_results[[female_FXL_k]] <- tibble(
      Longitude = female_FXL_chunk$Longitude, Latitude = female_FXL_chunk$Latitude,
      period = female_FXL_period_levels[female_FXL_k], period_num = match(female_FXL_period_levels[female_FXL_k], PERIOD_CODES),
      female_FXL_epred_median = female_FXL_q_period[2, ],
      female_FXL_epred_lower90 = female_FXL_q_period[1, ],
      female_FXL_epred_upper90 = female_FXL_q_period[3, ]
    )
  }

  female_FXL_q_all <- apply(female_FXL_mean_draws, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.05, 0.50, 0.95))
  female_FXL_all_period_chunks[[female_FXL_j]] <- tibble(
    Longitude = female_FXL_chunk$Longitude, Latitude = female_FXL_chunk$Latitude,
    med = female_FXL_q_all[2, ], low = female_FXL_q_all[1, ], high = female_FXL_q_all[3, ],
    period_all = "All represented periods (equal weights)"
  )
  female_FXL_period_chunks[[female_FXL_j]] <- bind_rows(female_FXL_period_results)
}

pred_all_masked_female_FXL <- bind_rows(female_FXL_all_period_chunks)
female_FXL_grid_7periods <- bind_rows(female_FXL_period_chunks)
# Retain the original object names; the actual number of rows is determined by the number of periods for which there are samples in the model
readr::write_csv(pred_all_masked_female_FXL,
                file.path(out_dir, "female_FXL_grid_all_periods_draw_average_CI90.csv"))
readr::write_csv(female_FXL_grid_7periods,
                file.path(out_dir, "female_FXL_grid_epred_primary_noSDC_median_CI90.csv"))
```

### 11. Optional sensitivity model including SDC commingled remains

```{r female-fxl-sensitivity}
if (run_sdc_sensitivity) {
  female_FXL_withSDC_data <- extraction_source %>%
    filter(sex == 1, !is.na(FXL)) %>%
    mutate(
      longitude_scaled = (longitude - female_FXL_longitude_center) / female_FXL_longitude_scale,
      latitude_scaled  = (latitude - female_FXL_latitude_center) / female_FXL_latitude_scale,
      mintemp_scaled   = (Mintemp - female_FXL_mintemp_center) / female_FXL_mintemp_scale,
      maxtemp_scaled   = (Maxtemp - female_FXL_maxtemp_center) / female_FXL_maxtemp_scale,
      minprecip_scaled = (Minprecip - female_FXL_minprecip_center) / female_FXL_minprecip_scale,
      maxprecip_scaled = (Maxprecip - female_FXL_maxprecip_center) / female_FXL_maxprecip_scale,
      altitude_scaled = (Altitude - female_FXL_altitude_center) / female_FXL_altitude_scale,
      FXL_z = (FXL - mean_fxl_female) / sd_fxl_female,
      period = factor(as.character(period), levels = female_FXL_period_levels), site_id = factor(site_id)
    )
  if (!any(female_FXL_withSDC_data$site_id == "SDC")) {
    stop("There are no SDC individuals available in the data containing SDC; please check whether the environment extraction needs to be re-run")
  }
  if (anyNA(female_FXL_withSDC_data$period)) {
    stop("SDC introduces time periods not included in the primary analysis; therefore, the comparison design must first be examined")
  }
  contrasts(female_FXL_withSDC_data$period) <- contrasts(female_FXL_main_data$period)
  fit_female_FXL_withSDC <- brm(
    formula = female_FXL_formula, data = female_FXL_withSDC_data,
    family = student(), prior = female_FXL_priors,
    iter = 4000, warmup = 1000, chains = 4, cores = 4,
    seed = female_FXL_seed + 10L, backend = stan_backend, control = brms_control, refresh = 500,
    file = file.path(model_dir, "female_FXL_sensitivity_withSDC"), file_refit = refit_mode
  )
  print(summary(fit_female_FXL_withSDC, prob = 0.90))
  female_FXL_sensitivity_diagnostics <- posterior::summarise_draws(
    posterior::as_draws_array(fit_female_FXL_withSDC)
  )
  female_FXL_sensitivity_nuts <- brms::nuts_params(fit_female_FXL_withSDC)
  female_FXL_sensitivity_sampler <- tibble(
    divergences = sum(female_FXL_sensitivity_nuts$Parameter == "divergent__" & female_FXL_sensitivity_nuts$Value > 0),
    max_treedepth_hits = sum(female_FXL_sensitivity_nuts$Parameter == "treedepth__" &
                              female_FXL_sensitivity_nuts$Value >= brms_control$max_treedepth)
  )
  print(female_FXL_sensitivity_sampler)
  if (any(female_FXL_sensitivity_diagnostics$rhat > 1.01, na.rm = TRUE) ||
      any(female_FXL_sensitivity_diagnostics$ess_bulk < 400, na.rm = TRUE) ||
      any(female_FXL_sensitivity_diagnostics$ess_tail < 400, na.rm = TRUE) ||
      female_FXL_sensitivity_sampler$divergences > 0 || female_FXL_sensitivity_sampler$max_treedepth_hits > 0) {
    warning("Convergence or sampling diagnostics for models involving SDC need to be checked")
  }
  readr::write_csv(as.data.frame(female_FXL_sensitivity_diagnostics),
                  file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_withSDC_diagnostics.csv"))
  readr::write_csv(female_FXL_sensitivity_sampler,
                  file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_withSDC_sampler.csv"))
  female_FXL_main_fixed <- as.data.frame(fixef(fit_female_FXL_main, robust = TRUE, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))) %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>% mutate(model = "primary_noSDC")
  female_FXL_sensitivity_fixed <- as.data.frame(fixef(fit_female_FXL_withSDC, robust = TRUE, probs = c(0.05, 0.95))) %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>% mutate(model = "sensitivity_withSDC")
  readr::write_csv(bind_rows(female_FXL_main_fixed, female_FXL_sensitivity_fixed),
                  file.path(table_dir, "female_FXL_SDC_fixed_effects_comparison.csv"))
}
```
